description: The VALUE clause's Format-3 WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase (ISO 13.18.63.2 format 3 - the bracket [ WHEN SET TO FALSE IS literal-4 ] printed on the line after [ IN alphabet-name-1 ]). literal-4 is the value 13.18.63.4 GR20 places in the conditional variable for 'SET condition-name TO FALSE', and 13.18.63.3 SR27 screens it against the condition's own VALUE set (COBOL2048). A COBOL-2002 addition, with the SET Format-4 FALSE phrase it exists to feed. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): ANSI X3.23-1985's condition-name VALUE clause is Format 2, `{VALUE IS | VALUES ARE} {literal-2 [{THROUGH | THRU} literal-3]}...` with no FALSE phrase (§1985:VI.5.15.5 GR2: 'Format 2 can be used only in connection with condition-names'), and its SET sets a condition-name only to TRUE (§1985:VI.6.23.2 Format 4: 'SET condition-name-1 TO TRUE'); §2002:13.16.61.3 GR17 reads 'When a condition-name is referenced in a 'SET condition-name TO FALSE' statement, the value of literal-4 from the FALSE phrase is placed in the associated conditional-variable' (§2002:13.16.61.2 SR19 screens literal-4), and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 144: 'VALUE clause, WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase in data division. The WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase allows specification of a FALSE condition value.' §2014:13.18.63.3 GR18 carries the same sentence, so 2014 = 2023. Recognition-fired by VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitValueClauseFalsePhrase: the binder abandons the operand on every 13.18.63.3 SR violation, so a bound-arm gate would lose the 0900 on exactly those paths (the TYPEDEF drop-proof lesson). kb/Work PB555.
display: the VALUE clause's WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase
